pr.title: Add project review setup, move, and census
pr.head: 2705222feafffedbc299bb08d9da9685c9ce5787

summary: Adds the first three project review commands from the review-scripts plan, so the mechanical steps of review-changes are tested code instead of gh snippets each loop session rebuilds: setup fetches the exact head into a scratch worktree and posts the start comment, move follows a head that moved mid-review by editing that comment in place, and census counts the Projector finding threads across every page.

review-changes/SKILL.md now runs these commands in place of its snippets, docs/cli.md documents them, and the plan moves from ready to in-progress. publish, the per-loop record, and review.gate are later delivery steps.

cards.title: Shared rules the commands enforce
cards.html:
• No command takes a SHA; each comes from GitHub or the state file.
  • Repository from --repo or the checkout's origin, passed to gh explicitly.
  • Posts use GH_TOKEN from gh auth token --user <reviewer> for that call alone.
  • Exclusive lock per pull request and head.
  • State under $XDG_STATE_HOME/projector/reviews; every refusal exits 1.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Review at 2705222: changes requested, 3 open threads — trailing blank line fails git diff --check; lock never released, so a re-review of an unmoved head is refused; fork pull requests refused with no other setup path.
  • Base review-scripts-plan (#127) has since moved to 1d8e4ce, revising forks, lock lifetime, worktree layout, and the per-loop record.

groups.title: The review module
groups.kicker: src/projector/review.py: identity, state, lock, setup, move, census
intro: One new module holds the three commands and their helpers. setup checks the pull request is open and same-repository, takes the per-head lock, fetches refs/pull/<n>/head and the base ref, verifies FETCH_HEAD and the worktree's HEAD against GitHub's SHA, then posts the start comment with a reviewer token and writes the state file.

move reads that state, refuses an unmoved head, locks the new head, edits the start comment, re-reads it to confirm, and hands the lock over. census pages the review-thread GraphQL query and keeps threads whose first comment carries projector-finding.
concepts: A lock is taken on success and released only on refusal or by move for the old head.
The state file is one per repository and pull request, not per loop.

checks.text: Every SHA the commands act on comes from pull_request() or the state file.
The reviewer token is passed only to the posting calls, never to reads or auth switch.
src/projector/review.py:228 — the lock is never released after a successful setup, so a RESPONDED re-review of the same head is refused.
src/projector/review.py:162 — fork heads are refused, and the skill no longer documents another way to set up their review; #127's revised plan fetches them and records them untrusted.

files.note: Read setup, move, and take_lock together for the lock lifecycle.

groups.title: CLI wiring
intro: Adds the review parser with setup, move, and census, shared --repo, --state-dir, and --json, and --checkout for the two that fetch. run_review discovers the checkout from the working directory and reads review.username from its configuration.

checks.text: An empty review.username falls through to the authenticated user.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Real Git against a bare origin, fake gh
intro: Sixteen tests run git for real against a bare origin holding refs/pull/1/head and replace run_gh with a recording fake, covering setup, token scoping, refusals, move, census paging, and that no command takes a SHA.

checks.text: No test covers a second setup on the same head after the first finished.

groups.title: Skill, docs, and plan
intro: review-changes/SKILL.md replaces its start-comment, moved-head, and thread-query snippets with the commands and keeps their rules as what the commands guarantee. docs/cli.md gains a section on project review, and the plan's status becomes in-progress.

checks.text: Every rule the removed snippets carried survives either in the command or in the prose.
